summary: Nested bouncer call stack: Y(a,b,c)->Y(a+2,b-1,c+3) per round; epochs grow x2.5-3; mod-3 gap cases
mechanism: Inner loop Y(a,b,c) = 1^a 001 (10)^b 11 (01)^c E>: each round a+2, b-1, c+3, eating 6 blank cells.
When b hits 0, E wipes the 1^a block and walks left (Return); the level to its left resumes the same loop.
When that gap runs out it calls the right level again: a call stack, so each epoch replays shrunken copies.

rules.cases: L0 ends in 0; tail form 63/63 too. Gap leftover 0/1/2 (mod 3) = 3 different call paths, not yet ruled

template.diff: 7 of 12 transitions (A1 B0 B1 D0 E0 F0 F1; halt moves F1->F0); no relabel/mirror does better; best in FractalType7v2/v3 is 8
template.note: Same architecture: S1 loop (Inc/Incs) + Empty_b return + P call + Column + Good invariant. Its S1/Inc configs do not carry over: 0/20 Inc, our machine halts in 6 steps from S1.

strategy: Copy TM20's skeleton, not its rules: prove XY/YX/XY1/YX1/Return with es + ind (Incs-style), define P u r r' (call returns 0^u), prove one Column lemma per gap residue mod 3, then a Good-style inductive invariant with inequality bounds on the column chain; init via chunks + native_compute; nonhalt via progress_nonhalt.
risks: Gap leftovers mod 3 vary in the run (start residues 1:41, 2:23, 0:17 of 81 runs); TM20 kept all counts = 0 mod 3. Invariant must track residues.
Epoch ratio alternates x2.5 / x3 (not affine), so only an inequality invariant can work; exact epoch map unknown.
Resisted mxdys's FractalType7 LLM batch; template is 7 transitions away, so new Column lemmas, not copy-and-modify.
